sheets.name: 00_README
rows: Universal Scientific Repository — Fully Normalized v3.0

Science-only canonical repository. Each definition is stored once; all many-to-many meaning is expressed through ID-based junction tables. Observations remain separate because values, conditions, uncertainty, specimen and time are distinct scientific records.
Canonical definitions are separated from assignments, applicability, evidence and observations.
The 17-level spine is navigational; scientific relations carry the actual semantics.
Expanded scientific variants deduplicated into one object registry.

sheets.name: 05_CLASSIFICATIONS
rows: Every classification or variant family is defined once. Placement, properties, objects and evidence are linked in junction sheets.
A field appearing in quantum field theory whose quantized excitations are particles; characterized by transformation properties, dynamics and couplings.
Classifies fundamental dynamical degrees of freedom
Field species, Lorentz/gauge representation, Lagrangian terms
Established theoretical framework with extensive experimental confirmation
The four-dimensional differentiable manifold with metric structure used to represent events, intervals and gravitation in relativity.
Locates physical events and encodes gravitational geometry
Dimension, topology, metric, curvature, causal structure
Established theory; ontology interpretation remains model-dependent
A particle with no experimentally established internal structure, represented by an irreducible particle state/field excitation in the Standard Model.
Separates fundamental particle species from composites
Mass, spin, charges, quantum numbers, interactions; experimental compositeness limits
Experimentally established classes within the Standard Model
A particle with half-integer spin obeying Fermi–Dirac statistics and the Pauli exclusion principle.
An elementary spin-1/2 fermion carrying color charge and fractional electric charge, occurring in six flavors.
Flavor, color representation, charge, mass, generation
Experimentally established indirectly through hadronic phenomena and scattering
An elementary spin-1/2 fermion that is a color singlet; charged leptons and neutrinos occur in three generations.
Flavor, charge, mass, generation, weak quantum numbers
A particle with integer spin obeying Bose–Einstein statistics.
An elementary boson associated with gauge interactions: photon, gluons, and W/Z bosons in the Standard Model.
Gauge representation, spin, mass, charges, coupling
The spin-0 excitation of the Higgs field associated with electroweak symmetry breaking.
Spin-parity, mass, couplings and decay channels
Experimentally established; interpretation within Standard Model
A particle-like bound state or resonance with experimentally established internal constituents or structure.
Constituent content, binding/resonance, total quantum numbers
A color-neutral composite state governed by the strong interaction and made from quarks, antiquarks and gluonic fields.
Baryon/meson class, flavor content, spin-parity, mass, lifetime
A hadron with half-integer spin in the ordinary three-valence-quark sector; includes nucleons.
A hadron with integer spin in the ordinary quark–antiquark sector.
Flavor content, spin-parity, mass, decay modes
A proton or neutron; a baryon that is a principal constituent of ordinary atomic nuclei.
Proton/neutron identity, charge, isospin, mass, magnetic moment
The positively charged central bound system of an atom, composed of protons and neutrons except for protium, whose nucleus is one proton.
Defines nuclear identity and atomic number
Z, N, A, nuclear energy state, spin-parity, binding and stability
A species of atom or nucleus specified by proton number Z, neutron number N, and nuclear energy state when necessary.
The smallest neutral entity retaining the chemical identity of an element, consisting of a nucleus and bound electrons.
A species of atoms whose nuclei all have the same number of protons; atomic number determines element identity.
Atomic number Z; element name and symbol
An atom or molecular entity having a net electric charge due to loss or gain of electrons or other specified charging process.
A charged entity formed from a single atom.
One atomic center and nonzero net charge

An electrically neutral entity consisting of more than one atom, or a molecular entity with a single atom only where explicitly permitted by nomenclature; normally defined by a distinguishable bound arrangement of atomic nuclei and electrons.
Atomic composition, connectivity, charge=0, molecular structure/state
Internationally established; exact wording varies by context
A charged molecular entity composed of more than one atom.
Multiple atomic centers and nonzero net charge
Any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, ion pair, radical, complex, conformer or similar chemically identifiable entity considered individually.
Provides the individual-entity level for chemical description
Constitution, isotopic composition, charge, electronic state, conformation as relevant
An ensemble of chemically identical molecular entities that can explore the same set of molecular energy levels on the experimental timescale.
Matter of constant composition characterized by the entities of which it is composed and by physical properties under stated conditions.
Separates substances from mixtures and specimens
A chemical substance composed of atoms of two or more chemical elements in fixed stoichiometric relation, subject to accepted nonstoichiometry conventions.
A material containing two or more substances not chemically combined in a fixed stoichiometric identity; may be homogeneous or heterogeneous.
A region of a material system that is uniform in chemical composition and physical state and separated from other regions by boundaries.
Classifies homogeneous portions and states of systems
Intensive state variables, composition, symmetry/order parameter
A finite aggregate of a countable number of atoms or molecules whose properties differ from isolated constituents and often from bulk matter.
Classifies finite aggregates between molecular and bulk regimes
Constituent count, composition, geometry, charge and binding
Established research class; boundaries can be conventional
A molecule of high relative molecular mass whose structure comprises repeated or complex subunits and whose properties depend on that high molecular mass.
A macromolecule containing multiple constitutional repeating units or derived from polymerization.
Repeat units, degree of polymerization, architecture
An organized association of two or more molecular entities maintained principally by noncovalent interactions and/or topological association.
Component identity, stoichiometry, interaction topology, cooperativity
A particle with external dimensions in the nanoscale, commonly about 1–100 nm, whose properties may be size- and surface-dependent.
External dimensions, morphology, composition, surface state
Matter selected or designed for use or study, characterized by composition, structure, processing, properties and performance.
Composition, phase, microstructure, form and function
A material possessing crystalline order in all or part of its volume.
A solid having an essentially discrete diffraction pattern; may be periodic or aperiodic.
A crystal whose structure has three-dimensional translational periodicity.
Translation lattice, unit cell, space group
A crystal with long-range order and discrete diffraction but without three-dimensional lattice periodicity.
Diffraction module/superspace description; absence of 3D lattice periodicity
An aperiodic crystal with quasiperiodic order, often showing symmetries incompatible with periodic lattices.
Discrete diffraction indexable in higher-rank modules; quasiperiodicity
A solid lacking the long-range translational or quasiperiodic order characteristic of crystals, though short-range order may be present.
Diffuse diffraction, glass transition behavior, local structure
Established; glass definition can be operational
A solid aggregate of many crystal grains separated by grain boundaries.
Grain population, orientations, boundaries and texture
The arrangement, size, morphology, distribution and interfaces of phases, grains, pores and defects at microscopic to mesoscopic scales.
Feature types, length scales, topology and statistics
A contiguous crystalline region with a substantially uniform crystallographic orientation.
A departure from the ideal reference crystal structure, including point, line, planar and volume defects.
Dimensionality, topology, chemistry and displacement field
A naturally occurring solid substance recognized chiefly by characteristic chemical composition and crystallographic properties under IMA rules.
Governs mineral names and species identity
Chemical composition, crystal structure, natural occurrence and nomenclature rules
A particular natural occurrence of matter instantiating one or more mineral species, commonly with impurities, defects, zoning or intergrowths.
Separates individual object from mineral species name
Species identity, locality, texture, composition and structure
A naturally occurring mineral-like substance that does not meet all mineral-species criteria, commonly because it lacks crystalline order or has poorly defined composition.
Keeps noncrystalline natural substances distinct from minerals
Natural occurrence, material properties, failure of mineral criteria
A naturally occurring consolidated or coherent aggregate of one or more minerals, mineraloids, glass or organic material, classified principally by origin, composition and texture.
Genesis, modal composition, texture, structure and chemistry
Established; schemes depend on rock family
Rock formed by solidification or crystallization of magma or lava.
Mode of occurrence, texture, modal mineralogy or chemistry
Rock formed by deposition and lithification of sediment or by chemical/biogenic precipitation at or near Earth’s surface.
Depositional origin, grain size, composition, texture and structures
Rock transformed in the solid state by changes in temperature, pressure, stress and fluid activity, producing new mineral assemblages and fabrics.
Protolith, mineral assemblage, texture/fabric and pressure–temperature history
Unconsolidated particles or chemical/biological precipitates transported or deposited by water, wind, ice, gravity or in situ processes.
Classifies mobile and deposited particulate material
Grain size, composition, sorting, shape, fabric and depositional setting
The layer of loose, heterogeneous material overlying coherent bedrock, including weathered rock, soil and transported deposits.
Position above bedrock, origin, degree of weathering and material type
A natural body at the land surface consisting of mineral and organic matter, water, air and organisms, organized into horizons by soil-forming processes.
Horizons, morphology, composition, climate/organism/relief/parent material/time effects
A body of rock defined and recognized on the basis of observable lithic properties and stratigraphic relations.
Maps rock bodies independently of age
Lithology, boundaries, stratigraphic position and mappability
The smallest formal lithostratigraphic unit, a distinctive layer within a member or formation.
A formal lithostratigraphic unit below formation rank, used for a lithologically distinctive part of a formation.
The fundamental formal lithostratigraphic unit: a mappable body of rock identified by lithic characteristics and stratigraphic position.
Mappability at chosen scale, lithic distinction, defined boundaries and type section
A formal lithostratigraphic unit comprising two or more associated formations or equivalent units.
A formal assemblage of related groups or formations used for very large stratigraphic packages.
A geometric arrangement or deformation feature in rock or sediment produced by geologic processes.
Geometry, kinematics, orientation, scale and cross-cutting relations
A fracture or zone of fractures across which there has been measurable displacement.
Slip, orientation, kinematics, geometry and timing
A curved or bent geologic surface or layered body produced by deformation.
Axial surface, hinge, wavelength, amplitude, orientation and vergence
A region of prolonged subsidence or accommodation in which sediments accumulate and are preserved as a basin fill.
Integrates subsidence, sediment supply, stratigraphy and thermal history
Basin geometry, subsidence mechanism/history, fill, boundaries and tectonic setting

A sedimentary/depositional basin containing regionally significant evaporite deposition and commonly later dissolution or salt deformation; ‘salt basin’ is descriptive rather than a universal formal rank.
Classifies basin systems dominated in part by evaporite accumulation/evolution
Evaporite volume/stratigraphy, brine restriction and concentration, basin setting, salt tectonics where present
A three-dimensional assemblage of genetically linked depositional environments and processes through which sediment is transported and deposited.
Process linkage, facies, sediment routing, environment and boundaries
A connected set of sediment sources, transport pathways, depositional sinks and recycling processes operating over defined space and time.
Source, flux, connectivity, storage, sink, grain-size and timescale
A geologic formation, group of formations, or part of a formation that is sufficiently permeable to transmit useful quantities of groundwater.
Hydraulic conductivity, saturated thickness, storage, connectivity and boundaries
A hydraulically connected set of aquifers and confining units functioning as a regional groundwater system.
Hydraulic connectivity, heads, recharge/discharge, aquifers and confining units
A groundwater domain defined by recharge areas, flow paths, storage, discharge areas and hydraulic boundary conditions.
Hydraulic head field, flow paths, boundaries, stores and fluxes
Flowing surface water within a natural channel, considered as water body, channel and process under specified scope.
Classifies fluvial flow and channel bodies
Channel geometry, discharge regime, sediment transport, network position
A connected network of channels, tributaries, floodplains and associated water/sediment fluxes draining toward an outlet.
Connectivity, drainage topology, discharge, sediment flux and outlet
The land area and associated surface and subsurface waters that drain to a specified outlet; terminology varies by jurisdiction.
Defines control volume for water and material budgets
Topographic or hydrologic divide, outlet, contributing area and nested scale
A bounded set of water stores, fluxes, phase changes and interactions across atmosphere, surface, subsurface and biota.
Boundary, reservoirs, fluxes, forcing, state variables and timescale
A spatially heterogeneous area composed of interacting ecosystems, landforms and land-cover patches at a scale relevant to the process studied.
Classifies spatial mosaics and cross-boundary flows
Patch mosaic, connectivity, relief, land cover, process scale
A region distinguished by coherent geologic history, structure, stratigraphy or tectonic character.
Boundary rationale, structural/stratigraphic coherence, tectonic history
A lithospheric plate and its boundaries/interactions, described within plate tectonics.
Classifies large-scale lithospheric motion and deformation
Plate boundary, velocity, rigidity approximation, interaction type
Established theory/model with observed plate motions
A molecule produced by or functioning in living systems, including nucleic acids, proteins, lipids, carbohydrates and metabolites.
Structure, biosynthetic/functional context, sequence or composition
A specialized subcellular structure with defined molecular composition and function, commonly membrane-bound in eukaryotes but not universally so.
Boundary/structure, molecular composition and cellular function
The basic membrane-bounded unit of life capable of regulated metabolism and biological information processing; cells may be organisms or parts of multicellular organisms.
Membrane boundary, metabolism, genetic system, reproduction/maintenance capacity
An organized ensemble of cells and extracellular material performing related functions in a multicellular organism.
Cell types, extracellular matrix, organization and function
A discrete body part composed of multiple tissues organized to perform one or more functions.
A functionally integrated set of organs and associated tissues within an organism.
Participating organs, connections, regulation and function
An individual living system with integrated organization, metabolism, regulation and a life cycle; individuality can be complex in colonial and modular life.
Unit for physiology, life history and population membership
Individuals of the same species occupying a defined area and time with potential demographic and genetic interaction.
Species identity, spatial/temporal boundary, demographic connection
Populations of different species occurring and interacting in a defined place and time.
A community of organisms together with the nonliving physical and chemical environment interacting through energy flow and material cycling in a defined area.
Boundary, community, abiotic environment, fluxes and processes
A large regional ecological unit characterized by climate, dominant vegetation or other broad biotic structure; marine biome schemes use different criteria.
Climate, vegetation/functional form, geography and disturbance regime
The global sum of living organisms and the regions of Earth where life interacts with atmosphere, hydrosphere and geosphere.
Extent of life, biomass, productivity and biogeochemical coupling
The gaseous envelope surrounding Earth, stratified by composition and thermal/dynamical structure.
Planetary gas reservoir and circulation system
Composition, pressure, temperature, circulation and vertical structure
All water in liquid form at or near Earth’s surface and subsurface, often used more broadly for all planetary water reservoirs depending on convention.
Water distribution, state, salinity, storage and flux
Earth’s frozen-water components, including snow, glaciers, ice sheets, sea ice, permafrost and frozen ground.
Ice/snow extent, mass balance, temperature and dynamics
The solid Earth, including crust, mantle and core and their geologic materials and processes.
Composition, structure, rheology, heat flow and tectonic dynamics
Earth considered as an interacting system of atmosphere, hydrosphere, cryosphere, geosphere and biosphere, driven by internal energy and external forcing.
Integrates planetary reservoirs, fluxes, feedbacks and evolution
Subsystem coupling, global budgets, forcing, feedback, state and history
A phase that sustains shear stress on relevant timescales and has a stable shape in the absence of external forcing; may be crystalline or amorphous.
Mechanical response, structure and phase behavior
A condensed fluid phase with no long-range shear rigidity at equilibrium, approximately fixed volume and ability to flow.
Fluidity, density, viscosity, local order and phase equilibrium
A compressible fluid phase that expands to fill its container and has relatively low particle density compared with condensed phases.
Equation of state, density, pressure, temperature and composition
A quasineutral ionized gas exhibiting collective electromagnetic behavior and screening over scales larger than the Debye length.
Distinguishes collective ionized matter from ordinary gas
Ionization, quasineutrality, Debye length, plasma frequency and collective response
Established; plasma-physics depth is an expansion area
A fluid above its critical temperature and pressure where liquid and gas are not separated by a first-order phase boundary.
T>Tc and P>Pc; continuous density variation
One of two or more nuclides having the same atomic number Z but different neutron numbers N and therefore different mass numbers A; isotope identity is always relative to an element.
Classifies variants of one element by nuclear composition
Same Z; different N (and A); nuclear state specified separately when needed
IUPAC-established; nuclear stability requires models and measurements
A metastable excited state of a nuclide with a measurable lifetime, distinguished from its ground state or other isomers.
Same Z and N; distinct nuclear energy state, spin-parity and lifetime
An assembly consisting of a central atom or ion, commonly metallic, surrounded by ligands with coordinate bonding interactions.
Central atom/ion, ligands, coordination number, geometry, charge and connectivity
An ion together with a specified solvation environment, usually represented statistically by ion–dipole, hydrogen-bonding and coordination interactions with solvent molecules.
Separates free-ion notation from solution-state structure
Ion identity, solvent, coordination/solvation number, exchange timescale and thermodynamic state
A crystal in which oppositely charged ions occupy an extended ordered structure stabilized substantially by Coulombic interactions, with additional short-range and polarization effects.
Composition, ionic sites/occupancies, space group, lattice plus basis, coordination and electrostatic stability
A mineral species whose essential chemical composition consists of one element, including polymorphs such as graphite and diamond for carbon.
Distinguishes mineral species in the native-element class from abstract chemical elements
Natural occurrence, single-element essential composition, crystal structure and IMA species criteria
Electrostatic interaction between charged chemical entities; in solids it is a collective, nonlocalized contribution to lattice binding rather than a set of isolated two-body bonds.
Charges, separation, dielectric environment, coordination, polarization and quantum-mechanical short-range terms
